newsitem.title: SPAIN: Clinton tours Spain's fabled Alhambra.
newsitem.headline: Clinton tours Spain's fabled Alhambra.

text.p: Stepping back into history after helping to point NATO towards the future, President Bill Clinton on Wednesday toured the fabulous Alhambra Palace, the seat of power of Spain's ancient Moorish rulers.

Accompanied by his wife Hillary, daughter Chelsea and a school chum, Clinton arrived at the palace fortress shortly before sunset, when its clay outer walks take on a reddish cast. Waiting to greet them was King Juan Carlos, Queen Sophia and their eldest son, Prince Felipe.

"I'm glad to be back ... It's just like I remember it," said Clinton, who earlier in the day ended a two-day NATO summit in Madrid at which leaders of the 16-nation alliance began an historic expansion eastward.
Clinton last visited the famous landmark in 1969 when he was a student at Oxford University in England. He told reporters and photographers: "You guys need to make the tour. Stop working."
"I'll give you an excuse: no news, culture!" he commanded.

Built by the Arabic-speaking Moors in the 13th and 14th centuries, Alhambra is considered a jewel of Islamic architecture, with its graceful fountains, ornate arches and halls of dazzling sumptuousness.
Perched on a hillside, it commands a sweeping view of Granada while the Sierra Nevada mountains tower in the distance behind it.

Alhambra was captured by the armies of Castilian Queen Isabella and King Ferdinand in 1491, and it was here that Isabella gave Christopher Columbus the money that financed the discovery of America there.

The U.S. first family and Spain's royal family posed for pictures briefly in the Court of the Lions, a small courtyard surrounded by an ornately decorated portico with two projecting pavilions. In the centre was a fountain surrounded by stone lions.

After their 45-minute tour, most of which was private, the Clintons and the royals motored to a square in the old section of Granada called Mirador de San Nicholas to watch the sunset and have dinner at a local restaurant. A large crowd lined the streets as their motorcade passed.
On Thursday, Clinton travels to Poland to help celebrate its selection as one of the first eastern European countries invited to join NATO. The others are Hungary and the Czech Republic.
His wife and daughter begin a separate trip that will take them to Austria, Portugal and the Azores.
